message.content:
This looks like a CBP ruling on Blue Q sticker sets. Vinyl stickers with a paper backing and adhesive are most likely classified in heading 3919 (self-adhesive plates, sheets, film, and other flat shapes of plastics). The alternative is heading 4911 (printed matter, including decals). Printed vinyl stickers with designs are often put in 4911.91 (pictures, designs, photographs), but heading 3919 applies to plastic articles whose printing is not the primary use. I recall a CBP ruling where decorative stickers of vinyl were classified in 3926.40 (statuettes and other ornamental articles of plastics). For die-cut vinyl stickers, I believe the more likely classification is 3919.90.5060, other self-adhesive flat shapes of plastic, in rolls not over 20 cm wide or otherwise. For sticker sets, the headings 3919 and 4911 compete, and Note 2 to Chapter 49 excludes products of heading 3918 or 3919. Printing that is not merely incidental to the primary use puts goods in Chapter 49, but 4911 only applies when the printing is the essential feature. For stickers, the printed design is the point, which would favor 4911.99. However, Chapter 49 Note 2(?) excludes plastic goods of 3918/3919 when the goods are otherwise covered by those headings. Because the stickers are die-cut vinyl with adhesive, I'll go with 3919.90.5060.
